exchanges.response: {"assessments":[{"factor":"F2","score":4,"justification":"Party-game obstacle courses map to the obby genre, which is already native to Roblox (leader at 20,000 players), and the tags 3D Platformer, Casual and Party Game fit; I stopped at 4 because the Battle Royale elimination format is slightly different.","confidence":"high"},{"factor":"F3","score":3,"justification":"Obstacle-course rounds with physics-based jelly-bean movement are easy to rebuild, but the Massively Multiplayer tag (60-player lobbies), elimination round variety and the course creator mean a full MVP needs several systems over 2 to 4 weeks.","confidence":"medium"},{"factor":"F4","score":5,"justification":"Chaotic eliminations and funny falls produce a clip every round (Funny, Party Game, Cute tags, 172,026 peak CCU), and Fall Guys-style content is already widely streamed and clipped.","confidence":"medium"},{"factor":"F6","score":5,"justification":"Battle Royale and Party Game tags indicate rounds of a few minutes, which is the 3 to 15 minute bracket.","confidence":"high"},{"factor":"F8","score":4,"justification":"Cosmetics (Cute, Colorful) are the natural fit, and extras like revives, boosts or emotes suit the round loop, but the competitive fairness of a party royale limits pay-to-win upgrades.","confidence":"medium"},{"factor":"F10","score":2,"justification":"The mechanic is generic, but the bean characters and the Fall Guys look are very recognisable and the owner is a major publisher (Epic/Mediatonic) that would likely file a claim against a literal copy.","confidence":"medium"}]}
